tasks.title: Define and prove Remote Runtime execution
tasks.objective: Add a real remote Backend only after Phase 1 fixes Runtime identity, capabilities, observation, waits, activation, and Integration ownership.
tasks.outcome: Clients can select a declared remote Runtime and preserve the same Run lifecycle contract without placing transport credentials or distributed orchestration in the core model.
acceptance: A reviewed architecture decision defines remote Runtime identity, transport, authentication owner, capability discovery, failure and reconnect semantics, process ownership, replay, retention, security, and supported platforms before implementation.
Remote execution remains a Backend axis; Integrations still describe what runs, while scheduling, fleet policy, credentials, collaboration, and evaluation stay above ctxmux.
Unsupported input, resize, signal, stop, replay, fork, persistence, or upgrade requests fail explicitly with no local fallback or fidelity downgrade.
Real remote-process lifecycle evidence proves client exit survival, reconnect, ordered output, terminal observation, bounded failure, and cleanup through the public protocol.

verification.proves: Remote protocol, security, lifecycle, reconnect, capability negatives, resources, and supported-platform gates pass.
Remote Backend ownership, trust boundary, guarantees, and non-goals are explicit.

tasks.title: Add Provider-neutral interrupted Run derivation metadata
tasks.objective: Expose the smallest generic derivation inputs and lineage needed for a caller to materialize a new Run from an interrupted one without claiming Provider-native resume.
tasks.outcome: An embedding client can inspect generic interruption and declared derivation references, choose policy externally, and submit an explicit new Run plan with honest lineage.
acceptance: The model records only Provider-neutral source Run identity, interruption reason, portable Run specification, declared references, capability requirements, and actual derivation fidelity.
Provider session IDs, semantic replay, prompt reconstruction, permissions, workspace state, message history, and native resume commands remain Integration or embedding-product data.
A request for richer derivation fails closed when the Integration cannot materialize it and never silently becomes Level A or an ordinary restart.
Cold restart, planned exec continuity, Remote Runtime reconnection, fork, and interrupted derivation remain separately named and tested lifecycle classes.

verification.proves: Derivation schema, lineage, failure fidelity, persistence, cross-language parity, and negative space pass.
Provider-neutral derivation and Provider-owned resume remain separate contracts.
